_description: Data provenance labels for all experimental results

multi_trial_crypto.csv.statistical_method: 95% CI via z=1.96, CV computed per trial

queue_validation.csv.notes: Service rate µ derived from measured verification latency

model_comparison.csv.justification: M/M/1 provides upper bound on wait times (conservative). M/D/1 provides lower bound. True system lies between these bounds. M/M/1 selected as primary model for worst-case analysis.

constrained_hardware.csv.scaling_source: Published benchmarks (mbed TLS, TI SDK, OpenSSL speed)

hardware_profiles.ARM_Cortex-M4: 168 MHz, no crypto accel, mbed TLS benchmarks
hardware_profiles.ARM_Cortex-R5: 600 MHz, no crypto accel, TI AM65x SDK benchmarks

constrained_hardware.csv.limitation: Scaling factors are estimates based on published benchmarks. Actual IED performance should be measured on target hardware for publication-grade results.

ablation_study.csv.method: M/M/1 queueing model with measured service rates

defense_modes.none: No defense — all attack traffic reaches verifier
defense_modes.mac_filter: MAC allowlist — drops 100% of unknown sources
defense_modes.full_xdp: Combined XDP defense (MAC + rate limit + sequence validation)

ablation_study.csv.xdp_note: XDP defense effectiveness values are MODELED (not measured on live XDP). The model assumes XDP drops packets before they reach the verification queue. This assumption is valid because XDP operates at NIC driver level, before any application processing.

attacker_capability.csv.method: Attacker capability tiers based on published packet generation benchmarks
assumptions: Attacker has physical or logical access to substation LAN
GOOSE is multicast over Ethernet (no routing/firewall between attacker and IED)
Packet rates based on AF_PACKET (Python), DPDK (C), and hardware generators
